title: Stamping Press Die Changeover SMED Optimization
problem: Changeover between Model-X and Model-Y hood panels took 85 minutes, causing severe batching and overproduction waste.
root_cause: Tooling bolts required manual ratcheting; hydraulic lines lacked quick disconnects; overhead crane waiting time was 25 minutes.
countermeasures: Implemented SMED: converted die bolt fastening to single-turn pneumatic U-clamps, pre-staged dies on dual-station turnover tables, and added quick-couplers for hydraulics.
results: Changeover time reduced from 85 minutes to 9.5 minutes (88.8% reduction). Lot sizes reduced by 50%, saving $160,000 in carrying costs.
keywords: changeover smed setup time press die stamping single minute exchange of die batching

title: SMT Electronics Assembly Line Balancing & Starvation Removal
value_stream: PCBA Electronics Surface Mount Tech Cell
problem: Line throughput stalled at 62 units/hour against customer takt demand of 80 units/hour. Severe operator idle time and workstation starvation at automated optical inspection (AOI).
root_cause: Component placement head on Machine 2 was overburdened (Cycle time 58s vs Takt 45s); inspection nozzle feeder experienced frequent micro-jams.
countermeasures: Re-balanced component placement library across Machine 1 and 2; installed dual-track feeder cassette; established 3-piece buffer FIFO queue before AOI.
results: Throughput increased from 62 to 84 units/hour. Line balancing efficiency improved from 68% to 94%. Zero downstream station starvation.
keywords: line balancing bottleneck starvation takt time cycle time smt placement throughput pacemaker

title: Order-to-Delivery Value Stream Lead Time Compression
problem: Total customer order lead time was 18 business days, while total hands-on value-add work was only 3.5 hours. Process Cycle Efficiency was a dismal 2.4%.
root_cause: Batch-and-queue scheduling: engineering releases, machining, hydrostatic pressure testing, and painting operated in weekly batched lots of 50 units with huge inter-stage queues.
countermeasures: Re-engineered value stream layout into a cellular U-shaped flow with a single-piece flow pull system triggered by electronic Kanban; created cross-functional cell operators.
results: Total lead time plunged from 18 days to 2.5 days (86% reduction). Process Cycle Efficiency (PCE) surged from 2.4% to 17.5%. WIP reduced by $420,000.
keywords: value stream mapping vsm lead time process cycle efficiency pce batch and queue pull kanban flow

title: Wire Harness Reverse Installation Defect Eradication via Poka-Yoke
problem: Operators occasionally inserted wiring harness connectors 180-degrees inverted, causing terminal pin deformation and intermittent short-circuits at testing (1,450 PPM defect rate).
root_cause: Symmetrical rectangular connector design allowed manual insertion force to bypass visual orientation labels under rushed shift conditions.
countermeasures: Level-3 Poka-Yoke design change: 3D-printed asymmetrical guide keying blocks on the mating jig, making inverted insertion physically impossible. Added automated continuity interlock light.
results: Defect rate dropped from 1,450 PPM to 0 PPM (Zero defects over 180,000 cycles). Avoided customer warranty rework penalties of $92,000.
keywords: defect poka yoke mistake proofing fmea connector insertion orientation rpn quality

title: 5-Whys Investigation on Hydraulic Pressure Fluctuation & Unplanned Stoppages
problem: Spindle feed rate intermittently stalled during heavy face-milling, triggering error E-402 and halting the cell 14 times per week (average 22 mins per stop).
root_cause: 5-Whys identified oil cavitation; oil level was low; pump was sucking air; reservoir sight glass was clouded by degraded synthetic fluid; preventative maintenance interval lacked sight glass cleaning protocol.
countermeasures: Cleaned hydraulic circuit, replaced clouded sight glass with high-visibility float tube, added digital pressure transducer interlock with automated low-level warning, updated TPM weekly standard work.
results: Unplanned machine stops dropped from 14/week to zero in 90 days. Machine Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) rose from 71.2% to 88.5%.
keywords: 5 whys root cause analysis rca machine downtime hydraulic pressure maintenance breakdown oee

title: Packaging Line Warehouse Gemba Walk Waste Elimination
problem: Packers logged over 8 kilometers of operator walking per shift, suffering physical fatigue and failing daily carton fulfillment quotas by 18%.
root_cause: Gemba walk spaghetti mapping revealed extreme Motion and Transportation wastes: corrugated carton blanks, bubble wrap, and label printers were located 30 meters away from packing stations.
countermeasures: Implemented Point-of-Use Tooling (POUT) and 5S workstation redesign. Positioned cantilever overhead gravity-feed carton racks and mobile thermal label dispensers directly at each operator station.
results: Operator walking distance slashed by 74% (from 8.2 km to 2.1 km per shift). Packaging throughput increased by 26%, meeting 100% of daily fulfillment targets.
keywords: gemba walk 8 wastes downtime motion transportation 5s walking fatigue operator ergonomics

title: Medical Sterilization WIP Reduction via Drum-Buffer-Rope Pull System
problem: Sterilization autoclave chambers were overloaded with WIP queues, creating average wait times of 36 hours and frequent expedited rush orders.
root_cause: Autoclave was treated as an isolated batch operation; upstream cleanrooms pushed finished packs as fast as possible regardless of autoclave capacity.
countermeasures: Established Drum-Buffer-Rope (DBR) scheduling from Theory of Constraints: established autoclave as the drum pacemaker, capped buffer at 4 hours of work, tied release rope to upstream bagging.
results: WIP waiting time reduced from 36 hours to 4.2 hours. Autoclave utilization increased from 74% to 93% without adding capital equipment.
keywords: theory of constraints toc drum buffer rope wip queue bottleneck sterilization pull scheduling

title: Paint Shop Surface Blemish DMAIC Project
problem: Surface orange peel and pinhole blemishes caused a 9.4% first-run scrap and rework rate, costing $210,000 annually.
root_cause: Analyze phase revealed gun voltage fluctuation and relative humidity swings exceeding 65% during afternoon shifts, altering powder charge adhesion.
countermeasures: Installed closed-loop electrostatic voltage controllers, sealed the pre-treatment booth with positive air pressure, and instituted daily standard work for ground-hook burn-off.
results: Rework rate dropped from 9.4% to 0.8%. Annual direct cost savings of $185,000 verified by corporate finance. Project transitioned into Control Plan.
keywords: dmaic charter project scrap rework powder coating paint defect quality yield six sigma
